findings.judgment: Privacy remains observer-specific; private None is not global absence. Authenticated domain completeness and separate relational observation-security obligations preserve DP02/DP11 scope.
Interface compatibility and stored identity are not semantic preservation. Evolution retains duties/privacy/recovery or requires applicable amendment authority; consistent with DP08–DP10.

Legitimate bases, intended verifier relation, compatible predecessors and well-founded composition are explicit; ledger uniqueness is separately required. No machine proof or implemented PCD construction asserted.

Common statement binding distinguishes ZK, MPC and TEE evidence; bare external threshold signature can bypass off-chain proof policy after threshold compromise. Federation/trust continuity remains explicit.

Atomicity is domain/effect-scoped; net balances do not substitute for consent/issuer liabilities. Partial outcomes and already-final effects survive recovery. DS04/07/08/15/18 support these research inferences.

caveats.point: Synthesis line21 uses present-tense kernel composes, but surrounding research-draft framing and line31 explicitly reserve implementation and proof. Read as target architecture, not implemented capability.

MPLR028 negative witness is an unauthorized semantic change; properly authorized amendments may change controllers or beneficiaries within the explicit evolution policy. Its required-behavior paragraph already makes this distinction.
MPLR024 synchronizer example is a comparative acceptance witness, not a claim Midnight implements Canton synchronizers or unconditionally settles all legs.

Acquisition totals and the 142-reference verification count in synthesis line13 are parent acquisition assertions, not independently recounted in this design review. All ten candidate file hashes were computed here.

claims.claim: The broad no-metadata-leakage language must be scoped: detailed ledger projections assume Ledger API-only observation; network/on-wire observation can reveal transaction shape, parties, encoding sizes, and confirmer information while transaction content remains confidential.

SCU compatibility permits changed choice controllers/bodies and interface instance/view implementations. Data/metadata compatibility is not semantic equivalence or preservation of old signed intentions.

Choice-body non-interface dispatch is statically selected by package dependencies; interface dispatch and eligible top-level commands use dynamic package selection. A fixed interface and v1 contract can return 1 or 2 under different preferred implementation versions.

SCU runtime conversions add absent optional fields as None and reject dropping populated fields; metadata and ensure are rechecked. Unchanged stored contract identity does not imply unchanged execution semantics.

Current Canton 3.x contract keys are not globally unique identity: multiple active contracts may share a key. Resolution prioritizes in-transaction creations, disclosures, then known contracts; None can also mean no visible contract.

The 2023 Daml paper presents Daml-LF formal typing/evaluation/authorization rules, runtime validation, and re-typechecking; this study finds no established machine-checked whole compiler/runtime theorem or proof-carrying ZKIRv3 compilation in the inspected paper.

The paper keeps serializable ledger data first order, admits unrestricted recursion, and motivates auth checks before contract evaluation to avoid leaking data through errors. These design choices do not establish finite ZK circuit execution or noninterference automatically.

The paper describes compiler/runtime/ledger layers and diverse trust assumptions; Daml language, Canton runtime/synchronization, Splice application standards, and a Midnight ZKIRv3 proof backend are separate assurance targets.
Package vetting is participant-side operational compatibility/admission. It is not a universal theorem proving program correctness and is not a model for discretionary Moriarty developer approval.

V2 allocation authorizes send/receive sides for an account, supports multiple legs and net funding, optional settlement deadline, explicit committed status, and opt-in iterated settlement. None and Some(empty funding map) have different iteration meanings.

V2 choices accept actors and delegate implementation checks. The interface declares nonconsuming choices but requires bodies to consume the allocation. The sample archives and recreates pending state; complete withdraw/cancel/settle transitions use different authority rules.

The V2 default batch helper checks executor actors, unique transfer-leg IDs, positive amounts, matching settlement/admin, duplicate authorizations, and exact equality of required and allocated transfer sides. It exercises all supplied allocations and returns their results.

AllocationResult includes Pending and Settled with optional successor allocation. Default batch execution returns these results without an explicit all-Settled result assertion; atomic execution of a call is therefore not by itself proof of successful economic DvP across arbitrary implementations.

Current multi-synchronizer documentation says transactions execute on one synchronizer after required input reassignment. Detailed reassignment is explicitly non-atomic, with pending assignment; introductory atomic wording conflicts with that detailed account.

Finance distinguishes holding transfers from custodian credit/debit and supports intermediated pass-through. A holding is not universally a bearer token: issuer/custodian liability and off-ledger backing remain separate economic obligations.

limitations: No implementation, proof build, hardware audit or live settlement acceptance.
